$comment: Authoritative dependency and execution declaration for zheref/bankai-handbooks, hand-authored at its Hatsu adoption (hatsu:tenkai, 2026-10-20) because nen shu detect finds no build marker in a prose repository and nen scaffold init proposes a lane only from one (tenkai section 4a). The dependency, halt and install blocks are the canon sibling's (zheref/hatsu nen/contract.json) carried verbatim, so this repository is judged by the same pin, bootstrap and no-improvisation rules as the rest of the estate; the project block is this repository's own. Where a copy of any value here appears in README.md, AGENTS.md, a rules file or a workflow, this file wins and the copy is the bug.
authority: THIS FILE IS THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the Nen dependency. Any version, ref, URL or command echoed in README.md, docs/, an agent definition or a SKILL.md is a convenience copy of a value that lives here. Where a copy disagrees with this file, this file wins and the copy is the bug. Read the values from here at run time; never act on a remembered version. There is exactly one copy of this contract, at nen/contract.json. A second file carrying the same pin would be a second source of truth, which is the thing this clause forbids.
summary: This repository depends hard on the Nen CLI, as every Hatsu-adopted repository does: every deterministic step is a Nen verb. The dependency fails closed with auto-install: out of the declared range or absent, the checksum-verified bootstrap runs itself; only if the bootstrap fails does the session halt with the exact command. A Nen-owned operation is NEVER improvised in prose.

dependency.name: nen
dependency.minimum_semantics: MAJOR.MINOR capability minimum, checked by nen shu tools against the installed binary and its compatibility floor. Raise it for either a breaking compatibility floor or a newly adopted feature unavailable in earlier releases. This repository adopts the pin its canon sibling (zheref/hatsu) holds at adoption, 0.22 / v0.22.0, so the two are judged by one nen: the 0.22 line's consumer notes are breaking (every 0.22+ build refuses a 0.21 pin at exit 5), and nothing here uses a verb newer than that. Move it with the sibling's repin, tag first (CON-13).

zero_major_caveat.applies_while: the installed and pinned majors are both 0
zero_major_caveat.rule: For a pin 0.A and installed build 0.B.z with compatibility floor 0.F, Nen accepts A <= B and A >= F, bounded by that build's own minor. This repository's minimum 0.22 with Nen 0.22.0/floor 0.22 is accepted; Nen 0.21.x is older than the required feature minimum, and a pin below 0.22 is refused by every 0.22+ build (a pin below 0.21 by every 0.21+ build, below 0.20 by every 0.20+ build, below 0.19 by every 0.19+ build, below 0.18 by every 0.18+ build, below 0.17 by every 0.17+ build). Legacy minimum 0.7 stayed compatible through Nen 0.16.x, but that never proved an older binary supports nen runner, nen canon pin, nen pr merge or nen wc swap. Read the exact range from nen shu tools. An unparseable version is unknown and unsatisfied, not a pass.
zero_major_caveat.why: SemVer 2.0.0 clause 4: at major version zero the public API is unstable and anything MAY change at any time, so at 0.x the MINOR is the breaking-change vehicle. Read at its strictest that made '0.7' mean '>=0.7.0 <0.8.0' EXACTLY, and every minor — breaking or not — owed a repin PR in every consuming repository; a repin owed unconditionally is a repin nobody reads. The maintainer's ruling of 2026-09-10 narrows it to 'exact minor is fine, unless there is a breaking change', and the fact that makes the distinction decidable is one the binary SHIPS rather than one a consumer infers: nen's release step sets COMPATIBLE_MINOR_FLOOR to a release's own minor when that release's CHANGELOG '### Breaking / consumer notes' section carries a real bullet, and leaves it where it stands when it carries none (zheref/nen#200; docs/USAGE.md 'the compatibility floor' and 'the release-time floor step', guarded by src/version.test.ts, which reads the topmost released section and fails the build when the two disagree). So the floor is what says which releases broke something, carried as data into a checkout that no longer exists rather than derived from prose at run time. It is a floor and never a ceiling, and it only ever WIDENS what is accepted — which is why nen's own notes for it record that it is not itself a breaking change. The floor is seeded at 0.7 because v0.7.0's notes ARE breaking, and those four changes are the reason the canon sibling's contract originally adopted minimum 0.7 (since raised, release by release, to the 0.22 this repository adopted at) at all: `nen stage triage` gained the `local-config` and `large` detectors, so a working copy that answered exit 0 answers exit 1 on the same bytes; every relative own-path flag resolves against `--repo`'s root instead of the PROCESS's directory, so one unchanged command line run from a worktree reads a different file; a missing or malformed `--target` exits 2 rather than 1 across sixteen verbs, and so does an unreadable caller-named input on `split verify`, `changelog` and `canon mirror check`; and `nen pr ready` READS `nen/gates.json`'s `dependabot_carve_out`, so a pull request that answered `not-ready` can answer `ready` against an unchanged file. Each is a silent change of meaning rather than a new flag, which is exactly what a floor exists to record.
zero_major_caveat.on_a_higher_minor: A newer release that keeps a compatibility floor admitting this feature minimum may satisfy the pin without a change. A raised floor above minimum requires an explicit compatibility repin. An installed binary older than minimum needs the published pinned_ref. Read the Nen verdict rather than downgrade a matching newer binary.
zero_major_caveat.from_1_0_onward: Once nen reaches 1.0, minimum 'X.Y' means >=X.Y.0 <(X+1).0.0 — backward-compatible WITHIN the major, so a higher minor or patch satisfies it and the compatibility floor is not consulted at all. nen already answers that way for a 1.x pin today; this contract is bumped to say so when nen's own line gets there.

dependency.pinned_ref_semantics: Bootstrap release ref v0.22.0, adopted 2026-10-20 as the canon sibling's current pin (zheref/hatsu nen/contract.json, whose pinned_ref_semantics narrates that pin's own history and verification; this repository carries the pin and its digests, not the sibling's narrative): darwin-arm64 sha256 872e2821abbd7cdc9c30ae402bb4e013ad78b116d421c16bad6e51f0426e02fa, linux-x64 sha256 c9b7ccb0bed158e081bdc92a7218da5a444b7fb4afb4a3ab85fa9e2cce846f37, windows-x64 sha256 911193135d1d8027ab952d10aa1c017f68b73342905b64ee9b6b132c7e47ca8c -- the digests of the binaries SHA256SUMS lists on that release, verified by Feitan against the asset at adoption. Move this ref, the three digests and dependency.minimum together, in one PR, after the sibling repins (CON-13: tag first).
dependency.pinned_ref_bootstrap_caveat: A TAG IS NOT A RELEASE, and this is the durable rule for EVERY value `pinned_ref` ever takes, not a note about one of them. `bootstrap/nen.sh` resolves the binary and its SHA256SUMS from the GitHub RELEASE at --ref; the tag's own tree carries the script but no assets. TWO CASES, AND THEY FAIL AT DIFFERENT STEPS. A `pinned_ref` whose TAG EXISTS but whose RELEASE is not published exits 6 (EXIT_MANIFEST — SHA256SUMS unfetchable) on both install_paths. A `pinned_ref` whose TAG DOES NOT EXIST YET NEVER REACHES EXIT 6 AT ALL: `raw.githubusercontent.com` 404s on the script itself, so `curl -f` exits 22 (or 56 mid-transfer), no file is created, and the second step never runs. Saying `exit 6` for both was wrong in a way that costs debugging time — an operator looking for a manifest failure when what is missing is the tag. Either way the warm-up halts per `halt`. That is the fail-closed guard working rather than a defect in this file, and exit 6 is one of the two codes that is NEVER retried. THE RULE THIS IMPLIES: never move `pinned_ref` to a ref whose release is unpublished without knowing that the halt is the cost. CI DOES SEE IT, and that sentence used to say the opposite: `.github/workflows/canon.yml` reads `dependency.pinned_ref` out of this file and bootstraps it, so a pull request that moves the pin ahead of the release goes RED at that step — `curl` 404s on the raw script, or the script exits 6 on an unfetchable SHA256SUMS — on every pull request, not only the one that moved it. That is the guard working where it can be seen rather than only on a developer's machine, and it is a reason to sequence the repin behind the release rather than a reason to weaken either. Publishing the release is the nen maintainer's act and the only thing that clears it.
dependency.version_probe_semantics: An argv ARRAY, never a string: nen's loader refuses the string form (verified: `at dependency.version_probe, expected an argv ARRAY, got the string "nen --version"`), because a string is one 'sh -c' away from a shell. The warm-up runs exactly these elements, with no shell in between.
dependency.version_probe_output: A bare semver on stdout, e.g. '0.10.0' — no 'v' prefix, no other text. The probe answers WHAT IS INSTALLED; whether that satisfies `minimum` is `nen shu tools`'s verdict and not this string's.

bootstrap.vendoring_forbidden: Hatsu never carries a copy of this script. A vendored copy is a second, unreviewed supply chain that drifts from the manifest it verifies against. Hatsu fetches nen's own published script at the pinned ref, every time.

sha256.$comment: The release digests of the pinned binary, keyed by platform. They mirror pinned_ref_semantics and move with the pin; scripts/nen_global.sh (the Hatsu plugin's host linker) refuses to link any binary whose sha256 differs, and a platform with no key here is never linked unverified. CI reads linux-x64: .github/workflows/canon.yml's taxonomy job hashes the bootstrapped binary and refuses one whose sha256 differs from this key -- main's copy where main carries this file, the head's on the adoption PR itself -- so a repin that leaves the digest behind fails every pull request after it.

fetch_must_be_two_step.rule: ALWAYS fetch to a file, then run that file. NEVER pipe the script into bash.
fetch_must_be_two_step.why: The script runs under `set -u` and reads ${BASH_SOURCE[0]}. Piped into `bash -s --` there is no BASH_SOURCE, so it dies with `BASH_SOURCE[0]: unbound variable` and exits 1 — a code that appears in NO table here, from a script that never reached its own argument parsing. It looks like an ordinary failure and is not one; it means the invocation form was wrong. Reproduced against this contract's pinned ref.

flags.--ref: Required, no default. The tag to pin to.
flags.--source: owner/name to fetch release assets from. Defaults to zheref/nen.

bootstrap.stdout: On success, the resolved and checksum-verified binary path — and nothing else. Execute exactly that path.

exit_codes.0: verified — the path on stdout is safe to execute
exit_codes.2: EXIT_USAGE — the invocation is wrong; nothing was attempted
exit_codes.3: EXIT_UNSUPPORTED_HOST — this platform/arch ships no nen binary
exit_codes.4: EXIT_DOWNLOAD — the binary asset could not be retrieved (the retryable one)
exit_codes.5: EXIT_CHECKSUM — SECURITY: bytes did not verify, or could not be verified
exit_codes.6: EXIT_MANIFEST — SHA256SUMS unfetchable, missing, malformed, or silent about the artifact
exit_codes.7: raised by `nen bootstrap` only, never by the script: no bootstrap/nen.sh found on disk. Not a supply-chain failure — a wiring failure. Supply --script.
exit_codes.curl 22 / 56 (before the script runs): THE SCRIPT ITSELF could not be fetched at the pinned ref and NO FILE WAS CREATED, so no exit code above was ever raised: `curl -f` exits 22 on the 404 and 56 on a mid-transfer failure. It means the tag or the release does not exist yet -- most often a pin moved ahead of the nen release. NEVER RETRIED: a tag that is absent now is absent on the next attempt. The fix is the nen release being published, which is the nen maintainer's act; nothing on this side clears it.

bootstrap.retry_policy: A curl 22/56 before the script runs is NEVER retried -- the tag or release is absent and will be until it is published. Exit 4 may be retried once. Exits 5 and 6 are NEVER retried — retrying a checksum failure is how a fail-closed guard becomes a fail-open one by attrition. Exit 3 will not change on this host. Exits 2 and 7 are invocation errors: never retry the same command, but the FIXED invocation (correct usage; for 7, supply --script) is expected to succeed — fix and re-run rather than halting on them.

halt.when: ONLY when the bootstrap itself fails (any non-zero exit above). An absent or out-of-range nen is not a halt — it is an auto-install.
halt.message_template:
Nen is unavailable and the checksum-verified bootstrap failed (exit ${EXIT_CODE} — ${EXIT_MEANING}). This operation is Nen-owned and will not be improvised. Run this yourself, then re-invoke:

    curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zheref/nen/v0.22.0/bootstrap/nen.sh -o /tmp/nen-bootstrap.sh
    bash /tmp/nen-bootstrap.sh --ref v0.22.0 --source zheref/nen

Two steps, never a pipe: the script reads ${BASH_SOURCE[0]} under `set -u`, so `curl … | bash` dies before it starts.
halt.after_halt: Stop. Do not perform the Nen-owned operation by another route — not with raw gh, not with a shell equivalent, not from memory. The operation does not happen.

install_paths.note: TWO cases, TWO paths. Which one applies is decided by the probe, never by preference.

nen_absent.when: `nen --version` is not found on PATH, exits non-zero, or prints something unparseable — and equally when the binary on PATH is so old it has no `nen bootstrap` at all (exit 2, `unknown command`), since the re-pin path below presupposes that verb.
nen_absent.why_shell_here: Chicken-and-egg, and it is the ONLY reason shell is permitted anywhere on this path. `nen bootstrap` is a nen subcommand, so invoking it presupposes the binary that is precisely what is missing. The script exists because a bootstrap written in the language its own output provides cannot run before that output exists. This is the sole carve-out; it does not generalize to any other operation.

nen_present_out_of_range.when: `nen shu tools --repo <this checkout>` answers the `nen` row `present-but-wrong-version` — the binary parses and does not satisfy `minimum` under dependency.zero_major_caveat's floor rule. The row is the verdict; the range is never recomputed here. TWO SHAPES, ONE PATH: a pin BELOW the build's compatibility floor (the row names the repin, and no build of that line will ever satisfy it — the fix is a pull request against this file, not an install), and a binary OLDER than the pin (the install below is the whole fix).
nen_present_out_of_range.path: Re-pin THROUGH NEN'S OWN VERB. A working nen is on PATH, so the chicken-and-egg rationale does not apply and the shell path is not the one to reach for.
nen_present_out_of_range.why_script_flag_is_required: VERIFIED, and it contradicts what the verb's name suggests: `nen bootstrap` does not fetch the script. It runs the checksum bootstrap rather than reimplementing it, so it needs bootstrap/nen.sh ON DISK — from a checkout carrying it (--repo) or named with --script / $NEN_BOOTSTRAP_SH. A Hatsu user has no nen checkout, so --script with the freshly fetched file is the form that works; without it the verb exits 7. Deliberate on nen's part: a compiled binary has no sibling bootstrap/ directory, and guessing one is how a nonexistent path becomes a silent failure.
nen_present_out_of_range.exit_codes: The verb propagates the script's codes unchanged — a forced failure through the verb returns 6, verified — plus its own 7 above.

no_improvised_fallback.rule: There is no LLM-improvised fallback for a Nen-owned operation, ever.
no_improvised_fallback.scope: A Nen-owned operation is any operation for which a nen verb exists — readiness determination, backlog fetch and ordering, board assembly and render, gate derivation, label application, an issue or pull-request comment (`nen issue comment`), changelog collation, fan-out computation, method-block validation, perf comparison, a target repository's declared build/test/lint/coverage/deploy (`nen shu`), and the rest of `nen --help`.
no_improvised_fallback.consequence: If nen is unavailable and the bootstrap failed, the operation does not happen. Reporting that is the correct outcome; substituting a hand-rolled equivalent is not.

no_jq.rule: Nothing on this path shells out to jq, yq or python to read this file.
no_jq.why: The ratified plan retires jq/yq as a DX friction — a machine needs one binary plus git and gh. And the reader here is an LLM agent that has already opened this file: parsing JSON by subprocess to hand values back to the entity that just read them buys a dependency for nothing.
no_jq.how_instead: Read this file, take the literal values, and issue plain curl / bash / nen commands with those literals substituted in. The one machine that also reads it is nen itself — `nen schema check --repo <this checkout>` — and that is a validation of the file, never a way of reading values out of it.

project.$comment: The one lane of a repository whose product is prose. nen shu detect proposes a lane only from a build marker it can see and this tree carries none (hatsu:tenkai section 4a), so the block is hand-authored, modelled on the canon sibling zheref/hatsu: the stack id is this repository's own name for what it is, validated against nothing, and every verb is either a real argv or a seat whose reason is quoted. `kind: process` is the repository's own word (docs/WORKFLOW.md section Repository kinds in zheref/hatsu): its releases are what every consumer pins, so hatsu:mugetsu executes the `release` row at G3 and hatsu:futon's advance go follows the process policy; hanten reads Nobunaga at the deep tier here.

canon.$comment: The repository lane: the constitution, the conventions and the handbooks under handbooks/, tokenised stack rules included, read as-is by every consumer's mirror renderer. Nothing compiles; the mechanical verification is scripts/canon_check.sh (redaction, links, taxonomy), which is what the `lint` verb runs and what .github/workflows/canon.yml runs job by job.

canon-check-guard.$comment: The focused lane for scripts/canon_check.sh, the lane's lint guard, following the canon sibling's one-lane-per-executable-guard pattern: its test is the script's own --self-test (every detector, allow-list, scan-set, link and exit-code claim as a negative or positive assertion in throwaway git repositories under mktemp). hatsu:tsukuyomi runs it on every turn that changes scripts/canon_check.sh, hatsu:hanten before a raise, and canon.yml's self-test job on every PR; it is not a general suite and is not an iteration check.

lint.$comment: The three checks a public canon repository can silently get wrong, in one script: no private repository name, slug or linked object id (docs/PUBLIC-REDACTION.md), every relative markdown link resolves, and nen schema check reads every nen/ file ok. It is the single iteration check nen/workflow.json declares: breath proves it on the fresh tip, rasengan runs it while authoring, kokusen refuses a red tree before every commit. CI runs the same script per job in .github/workflows/canon.yml.

build.unsupported: There is nothing to compile: the handbooks are markdown read as-is. `lint` (scripts/canon_check.sh) is the closest thing to a build and is declared as lint, where it belongs.

test.unsupported: No general test suite exists and none is owed: the canon's correctness is reviewed (Chrollo against UZF-, Nobunaga against the conventions), not executed. The one executable here, scripts/canon_check.sh, has its own focused lane (canon-check-guard) whose test is its --self-test; declaring a general runner that does not exist would make an unperformed check read as a clean one.

ui-test.unsupported: This repository renders nothing. A UX reviewer cites UX-{n} against a consumer's screens, never against this tree.

coverage.unsupported: Prose has no line coverage. byakugan reports touched files as `not measurable here` against the ladder in nen/workflow.json, which is declared so there is a ladder to report against; nothing reads it from this repository.

archive.unsupported: The tag IS the distribution: a consumer pins a tag of this repository (`nen canon pin`) and renders its mirror from that tag (CON-13). There is no artifact for `archive` to name, so hatsu:susanoo has nothing to build and hatsu:getsuga's release unit is the tag alone.

release.$comment: The real release row a process repository owes (hatsu:tenkai section 6a): publish ONE GitHub Release for a tag that already resolves on the remote, notes and title taken from CHANGELOG.md's section for that tag, no asset (archive is unsupported above, so none is handed in). The script is RENDERED by hatsu:tenkai from its templates/release-publish.sh and re-rendered on every re-adoption; hand-edits read as drift. Run only by hatsu:mugetsu on the maintainer's typed go (G3, CON-6), after hatsu:getsuga has cut the tag. KNOWN LIMIT at adoption (zheref/hatsu#362): the rendered publisher matches a tag's notes only at `## <tag>` while this CHANGELOG.md anchors on `### Unreleased` and nen changelog collate writes `### vX.Y.Z` sections, so `--dry-run` refuses `no '## v0.6.0' section` for every tag this repository can produce until the template reads the changelog's own heading level and this copy is re-rendered; the row stays real rather than seated so mugetsu's first G3 run meets a named refusal, never silence -- at the publishing call, since `nen shu release --dry-run` (the plan step) prints only the argv and never runs the script's own --dry-run.

dev.unsupported: Nothing here runs as a process. Reading the canon is opening a file; exercising it is a consumer's build against its mirror.

run.unsupported: Same as `dev`: there is no production build to start.

deploy.unsupported: Canon is not sent anywhere: a consumer pulls a tag through `nen canon pin` and renders its own mirror. There is no destination for --target to name, and `project.targets` is empty deliberately rather than by omission.

test.$comment: Exit 0 when every assertion holds, 1 on the first failed assertion, 2 when mktemp fails. Hermetic and offline: no nen is needed for the assertions that expect nen absent, which strip PATH themselves.

lint.unsupported: The guard IS the lint; this lane exists only to run its self-test. `nen shu lint --repo .` on the default lane is the check.

build.unsupported: Nothing to build: one bash script.

hosts.$comment: scripts/canon_check.sh is bash with grep, sed and nen; it is proved on Darwin (the maintainer's machine) and Linux (ubuntu-latest in canon.yml). Native Windows is not a declared host for this lane.

canon.why: The manifest every consumer resolves the handbook set through; a tree without it is not the canon this lane declares, and a lint over it would fail on a missing file rather than on a real defect.
The redaction policy scripts/canon_check.sh enforces; the check is meaningless where the policy it cites is absent.
